title: Ordinary realization of the completed coefficient unit

source.place: paragraph (1), preservation of coefficient-one maps under normalized realization, before applying any derived functor

statement: Let l be prime, Y a scheme, and P its projective line. Let eY and eP be completed coefficient realizations [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-reference]. Let ordinary be an isomorphism between completed direct image followed by eY.F and eP.F followed by condensed direct image, whose underlying sheaf equation is the prescribed ordinary_normalization. Then realization of the actual completed coefficient unit [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-finite-evaluation], followed by ordinary and direct image of eP.unitIso, equals eY.unitIso followed by the ordinary condensed coefficient unit [def-diagonal-coefficient-unit-push]. This is a statement about ordinary module sheaves, with no local class, shift, derived functor, limit square or normalized adjunct pair.

proof.text: The canonical comparison from a constant commutative ring sheaf, after forgetting to abelian sheaves, to the constant abelian sheaf preserves the internal unit. Its inverse is the sheafification of the ring-sheafification unit followed by the sheafification counit. Both are monoid morphisms. Identify that inverse by the constant/forgetful comparison unit equation.

Combine the underlying-sheaf comparison of a realization with its unitIso to obtain an isomorphism v from the actual completed coefficient sheaf to the condensed coefficient object. Precompose the unit of the condensed object with v inverse. At every positive finite projection, unit_normalization identifies the resulting map with the unit of the finite constant ring. The preceding comparison and all coefficient projections preserve one. The forgetful functor from commutative ring sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves limits, so these projections jointly detect equality. Hence v inverse preserves one, and therefore v preserves one.

The completedPushUnit is the underlying additive map of the structural coefficient ring map, so it preserves the internal unit. This follows directly from unitToPushforwardObjUnit on sections and compatibility of the monoid structure with sheaf direct image.

Precompose the desired module identity with eY.unitIso inverse and apply regular_hom_ext. Naturality of the underlying comparison and the ordinary normalization replace the left side by the actual completed unit map, conjugated by vY inverse and direct image of vP. The two unit-preservation identities just proved reduce it to the internal unit of the condensed direct image. coefficientOrdinaryUnit_underlying identifies the right side with the unital condensed structural coefficient map. Thus both maps agree on one, proving equality of regular-module maps, including on the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem completed_ordinary_unit
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (eY : CompletedRealization l Y) (eP : CompletedRealization l (ProjectiveLine Y))
    (ordinary : diagonalTracePush l (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) ⋙ eY.F ≅
      eP.F ⋙ CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} ℤ_[l])
        (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y))
    (hordinary : ∀ M : DiagonalCompleted l (ProjectiveLine Y),
      HEq ((ordinary.hom.app M).hom ≫
        (lowerStar Ab.{u + 1} (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map (eP.underlying.hom.app M))
        (eY.underlying.hom.app ((diagonalTracePush l (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).obj M))) :
    eY.F.map (DiagonalTrace.completedPushUnit l (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)) ≫
        ordinary.hom.app _ ≫
          (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} ℤ_[l])
            (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map eP.unitIso.hom =
      eY.unitIso.hom ≫ coefficientOrdinaryUnit _ Y
